svg.title: Moral evaluation combines what an actor believed with what happened
svg.desc: Three panels. A: a two-by-two matrix crossing the actor's belief (believes harmless, believes harmful) with the outcome (harmless, harmful). Each cell shows the same illustrative scene: a standing adult adds a spoonful of white powder from an unlabelled jar to a seated adult's drink. A thought card above the actor reads Thinks: harmless or Thinks: harmful; an outcome card beside the recipient reads No harm or Harm, with a small medical cross for harm. Cells: no harm; accidental harm; attempted harm; intentional harm. Matched illustrative stories, not original task stimuli. B: three independent study rows with qualitative contrasts. rTPJ TMS versus control site (Young et al., 2010): attempted harm more permissible; accidental harm no reliable pairwise shift. vmPFC lesions versus controls (Young et al., 2010): attempted harm more permissible; accidental harm no reliable difference. vmPFC lesions versus controls (Ciaramelli et al., 2012): attempted harm more permissible; accidental harm less permissible. Permissibility judgments, not measured helping or aggression. C: switch and footbridge schematics. In the switch case a trolley approaches a junction with five people on the continuing track and one on the branch; a bystander stands at a lever connected to the switch; a dashed arrow marks the possible diversion. In the footbridge case a trolley approaches five people; a bystander stands on a bridge beside one other person; a dashed arrow begins beside the person who could be pushed and marks the contemplated push onto the track ahead of the trolley. The arrows depict possible actions, not recorded decisions to act or refrain. One death to prevent five; both require action; they differ in personal force, causal role, and using a person as a means. Separate note: vmPFC lesions were associated with more endorsement of harm in selected high-conflict dilemmas.

g.text: Belief and outcome can vary independently
Matched illustrative stories; not original task stimuli
Permissibility judgments; not measured helping or aggression
rTPJ: right temporoparietal junction; vmPFC: ventromedial prefrontal cortex
One death to prevent five — both require action
